# IO list

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:io-list` from shared/channels.ts. Do not edit by hand. -->

70 monitored points. W = warning limit, C = critical limit. Points marked "blocked by" have their alarms suppressed while that machine is stopped.

## Main Engine

Slow-speed two-stroke diesel driving the fixed-pitch propeller directly.

| Tag | Point | Range | Unit | Alarm limits | Source | Address | Why it is monitored |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ME.SPEED` | ME speed | 0 … 140 | rpm | W ≥ 126, C ≥ 130 | Modbus TCP | ECS IR 30001 | Crankshaft speed from the engine control system. Overspeed (105% / 108% of MCR speed) precedes the overspeed trip. |
| `ME.LOAD` | ME load | 0 … 110 | % MCR | W ≥ 100, C ≥ 105 | Modbus TCP | ECS IR 30002 | Engine load as a share of maximum continuous rating. Running above 100% MCR overloads the engine. |
| `ME.SHAFT.POWER` | Shaft power | 0 … 9000 | kW |  | Modbus TCP | Torsionmeter IR 30010 | Power delivered to the propeller shaft, measured by the torsionmeter. Basis for SFOC and EEXI/CII reporting. |
| `ME.FO.FLOW` | ME fuel flow | 0 … 2000 | kg/h |  | Modbus TCP | Coriolis FM IR 30020 | Mass fuel flow to the main engine from the Coriolis flowmeter (supply minus return). |
| `ME.SFOC` | SFOC | 140 … 240 | g/kWh |  | Calculated | 1-min avg ME.FO.FLOW / ME.SHAFT.POWER | Specific fuel oil consumption over a one-minute window. The single best indicator of engine efficiency; a rising trend means fouling, worn injectors or bad fuel. |
| `ME.LO.PRESS` | LO inlet pressure | 0 … 6 | bar | W ≤ 3.4, C ≤ 2.9 | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC AI 1.01 | Main lube oil pressure at the engine inlet. Low pressure starves bearings; the engine slows down and then shuts down. |
| `ME.LO.TEMP` | LO inlet temp | 20 … 80 | °C | W ≥ 55, C ≥ 60 | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC AI 1.02 | Lube oil temperature after the LO cooler. High temperature thins the oil film. |
| `ME.HT.TEMP` | HT CW outlet temp | 20 … 110 | °C | W ≥ 90, C ≥ 95 | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC AI 1.03 | Jacket (high-temperature) cooling water leaving the engine. Held near 82 °C by the thermostatic valve. |
| `ME.THRUST.TEMP` | Thrust bearing temp | 20 … 100 | °C | W ≥ 75, C ≥ 80 | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC AI 1.04 | Thrust bearing pad temperature. It carries the whole propeller thrust; a rise means lubrication trouble. |
| `ME.SCAV.PRESS` | Scavenge air pressure | 0 … 4 | bar |  | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC AI 1.05 | Charge air pressure in the scavenge receiver. Falls when the turbocharger or air cooler is fouled. |
| `ME.SCAV.TEMP` | Scavenge air temp | 20 … 90 | °C | W ≥ 55, C ≥ 65 | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC AI 1.06 | Charge air temperature after the air cooler. A sudden rise is the classic sign of a scavenge space fire. |
| `ME.TC.SPEED` | Turbocharger speed | 0 … 20000 | rpm | W ≥ 18500, C ≥ 19500 | Modbus TCP | ECS IR 30030 | Turbocharger rotor speed. Overspeed damages the rotor; a drop at constant load points to fouling. |
| `ME.EXH.CYL1` | Exh temp cyl 1 | 100 … 550 | °C | W ≥ 420, C ≥ 450 | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC AI 2.01 | Exhaust gas temperature after the cylinder. Comparing cylinders exposes a leaking injector or burnt exhaust valve. |
| `ME.EXH.CYL2` | Exh temp cyl 2 | 100 … 550 | °C | W ≥ 420, C ≥ 450 | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC AI 2.02 | Exhaust gas temperature after the cylinder. Comparing cylinders exposes a leaking injector or burnt exhaust valve. |
| `ME.EXH.CYL3` | Exh temp cyl 3 | 100 … 550 | °C | W ≥ 420, C ≥ 450 | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC AI 2.03 | Exhaust gas temperature after the cylinder. Comparing cylinders exposes a leaking injector or burnt exhaust valve. |
| `ME.EXH.CYL4` | Exh temp cyl 4 | 100 … 550 | °C | W ≥ 420, C ≥ 450 | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC AI 2.04 | Exhaust gas temperature after the cylinder. Comparing cylinders exposes a leaking injector or burnt exhaust valve. |
| `ME.EXH.CYL5` | Exh temp cyl 5 | 100 … 550 | °C | W ≥ 420, C ≥ 450 | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC AI 2.05 | Exhaust gas temperature after the cylinder. Comparing cylinders exposes a leaking injector or burnt exhaust valve. |
| `ME.EXH.CYL6` | Exh temp cyl 6 | 100 … 550 | °C | W ≥ 420, C ≥ 450 | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC AI 2.06 | Exhaust gas temperature after the cylinder. Comparing cylinders exposes a leaking injector or burnt exhaust valve. |
| `ME.RUN.HOURS` | Running hours | 0 … 200000 | h |  | Modbus TCP | ECS IR 30040 | Total running hours. Drives the planned maintenance schedule (overhauls, liner calibration). |

## Generators

Three diesel generator sets on one 440 V bus, managed by the power management system (PMS).

| Tag | Point | Range | Unit | Alarm limits | Source | Address | Why it is monitored |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DG1.RUN` | DG1 running | 0/1 |  |  | Modbus TCP | PMS DI 10001 | Engine running and breaker closed. Blocks the engine alarms while the set is stopped. |
| `DG1.TRIP` | DG1 shutdown | 0/1 |  | Critical when 1 | Modbus TCP | PMS DI 10011 | Safety system shut the set down and opened its breaker. Load jumps onto the remaining sets. |
| `DG1.LOAD` | DG1 load | 0 … 1100 | kW | W ≥ 900, C ≥ 1000 | Modbus TCP | PMS IR 30101 | Active power from the set (rated 1,000 kWe). Above 90% the PMS starts the standby set. |
| `DG1.SPEED` | DG1 speed | 0 … 2000 | rpm | W ≥ 1900, C ≥ 1960 | J1939 | PGN 61444 SPN 190 SA 0x00 | Engine speed from the genset ECU (EEC1). 1,800 rpm gives 60 Hz. |
| `DG1.HT.TEMP` | DG1 coolant temp | 20 … 110 | °C | W ≥ 95, C ≥ 100 | J1939 | PGN 65262 SPN 110 SA 0x00 | Engine coolant temperature from the ECU (ET1). Standby sets are kept preheated so they can take load at once. |
| `DG1.LO.PRESS` | DG1 LO pressure | 0 … 8 | bar | W ≤ 3, C ≤ 2.5; blocked by DG1.RUN | J1939 | PGN 65263 SPN 100 SA 0x00 | Engine oil pressure from the ECU (EFL/P1). Blocked while the set is stopped, when zero pressure is normal. |
| `DG2.RUN` | DG2 running | 0/1 |  |  | Modbus TCP | PMS DI 10002 | Engine running and breaker closed. Blocks the engine alarms while the set is stopped. |
| `DG2.TRIP` | DG2 shutdown | 0/1 |  | Critical when 1 | Modbus TCP | PMS DI 10012 | Safety system shut the set down and opened its breaker. Load jumps onto the remaining sets. |
| `DG2.LOAD` | DG2 load | 0 … 1100 | kW | W ≥ 900, C ≥ 1000 | Modbus TCP | PMS IR 30102 | Active power from the set (rated 1,000 kWe). Above 90% the PMS starts the standby set. |
| `DG2.SPEED` | DG2 speed | 0 … 2000 | rpm | W ≥ 1900, C ≥ 1960 | J1939 | PGN 61444 SPN 190 SA 0x01 | Engine speed from the genset ECU (EEC1). 1,800 rpm gives 60 Hz. |
| `DG2.HT.TEMP` | DG2 coolant temp | 20 … 110 | °C | W ≥ 95, C ≥ 100 | J1939 | PGN 65262 SPN 110 SA 0x01 | Engine coolant temperature from the ECU (ET1). Standby sets are kept preheated so they can take load at once. |
| `DG2.LO.PRESS` | DG2 LO pressure | 0 … 8 | bar | W ≤ 3, C ≤ 2.5; blocked by DG2.RUN | J1939 | PGN 65263 SPN 100 SA 0x01 | Engine oil pressure from the ECU (EFL/P1). Blocked while the set is stopped, when zero pressure is normal. |
| `DG3.RUN` | DG3 running | 0/1 |  |  | Modbus TCP | PMS DI 10003 | Engine running and breaker closed. Blocks the engine alarms while the set is stopped. |
| `DG3.TRIP` | DG3 shutdown | 0/1 |  | Critical when 1 | Modbus TCP | PMS DI 10013 | Safety system shut the set down and opened its breaker. Load jumps onto the remaining sets. |
| `DG3.LOAD` | DG3 load | 0 … 1100 | kW | W ≥ 900, C ≥ 1000 | Modbus TCP | PMS IR 30103 | Active power from the set (rated 1,000 kWe). Above 90% the PMS starts the standby set. |
| `DG3.SPEED` | DG3 speed | 0 … 2000 | rpm | W ≥ 1900, C ≥ 1960 | J1939 | PGN 61444 SPN 190 SA 0x02 | Engine speed from the genset ECU (EEC1). 1,800 rpm gives 60 Hz. |
| `DG3.HT.TEMP` | DG3 coolant temp | 20 … 110 | °C | W ≥ 95, C ≥ 100 | J1939 | PGN 65262 SPN 110 SA 0x02 | Engine coolant temperature from the ECU (ET1). Standby sets are kept preheated so they can take load at once. |
| `DG3.LO.PRESS` | DG3 LO pressure | 0 … 8 | bar | W ≤ 3, C ≤ 2.5; blocked by DG3.RUN | J1939 | PGN 65263 SPN 100 SA 0x02 | Engine oil pressure from the ECU (EFL/P1). Blocked while the set is stopped, when zero pressure is normal. |
| `MSB.LOAD` | Total electrical load | 0 … 3000 | kW |  | Modbus TCP | PMS IR 30110 | Sum of all consumers on the main switchboard: reefers, pumps, fans, compressors, hotel load. |
| `MSB.FREQ` | Bus frequency | 55 … 65 | Hz | W ≤ 58.8, C ≤ 58 | Modbus TCP | PMS IR 30111 | Main bus frequency. It sags when the running sets are overloaded, the step before a blackout. |
| `MSB.VOLT` | Bus voltage | 380 … 500 | V | W ≤ 425, C ≤ 410 | Modbus TCP | PMS IR 30112 | Main bus voltage (440 V nominal), held by the generator AVRs. |
| `PMS.STBY.START` | Standby start | 0/1 |  | Caution when 1 | Modbus TCP | PMS DI 10020 | The power management system has started, synchronised and connected the standby set. |
| `PMS.LOAD.SHED` | Load shedding | 0/1 |  | Warning when 1 | Modbus TCP | PMS DI 10021 | Preferential trip: non-essential consumers are disconnected to save the bus from overload. |

## Fuel System

Heavy fuel treatment: purifiers, service tank, booster pumps and the viscosity-controlled heater.

| Tag | Point | Range | Unit | Alarm limits | Source | Address | Why it is monitored |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `FO.VISC` | FO viscosity | 0 … 40 | cSt | W ≥ 17, C ≥ 20 | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC AI 3.01 | Heavy fuel viscosity at the engine inlet. Injectors need 10-15 cSt; too viscous fuel atomises badly. |
| `FO.TEMP` | FO inlet temp | 20 … 160 | °C |  | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC AI 3.02 | Fuel temperature after the steam heater. The viscosity controller moves it to hold viscosity. |
| `FO.BOOST.PRESS` | Booster pressure | 0 … 12 | bar | W ≤ 6.5, C ≤ 5.5 | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC AI 3.03 | Fuel supply pressure to the engine fuel pumps from the booster (circulating) pumps. |
| `FO.SERV.LEVEL` | Service tank level | 0 … 100 | % | W ≤ 35, C ≤ 20 | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC AI 3.04 | Daily service tank, topped up continuously by the purifiers. A falling level means a purifier has stopped. |
| `FO.TOTAL.FLOW` | Total fuel flow | 0 … 2500 | kg/h |  | Calculated | ME.FO.FLOW + generator consumption | Whole-ship fuel consumption: main engine plus generator sets. |
| `FO.ROB` | Fuel remaining on board | 0 … 1500 | t |  | Calculated | bunkers - consumption | Remaining on board. Planned against the distance to go so the ship never runs short. |

## Cooling Water

Central cooling: sea water cools the LT fresh-water circuit, which cools everything else.

| Tag | Point | Range | Unit | Alarm limits | Source | Address | Why it is monitored |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SW.PRESS` | SW pump discharge | 0 … 4 | bar | W ≤ 1.4, C ≤ 1 | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC AI 4.01 | Sea water cooling pump pressure. Loss of sea water means loss of all engine-room cooling. |
| `SW.TEMP` | Sea water temp | -2 … 35 | °C |  | NMEA 2000 | PGN 130312 source 0 | Sea temperature. Sets how much heat the central coolers can reject. |
| `LT.TEMP` | LT CW temp | 10 … 60 | °C | W ≥ 40, C ≥ 45 | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC AI 4.02 | Low-temperature fresh water after the central cooler. It cools the LO cooler, air cooler and auxiliaries. |
| `LT.PRESS` | LT CW pressure | 0 … 5 | bar | W ≤ 1.8, C ≤ 1.4 | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC AI 4.03 | LT circuit pressure. A slow fall means a leak or an empty expansion tank. |

## Steering Gear

Electro-hydraulic rudder actuator with two pump units.

| Tag | Point | Range | Unit | Alarm limits | Source | Address | Why it is monitored |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SG.RUDDER` | Rudder angle | -35 … 35 | ° |  | NMEA 2000 | PGN 127245 position | Rudder position feedback, starboard positive. Shows how hard the autopilot works to hold the course. |
| `SG.HYD.PRESS` | Hydraulic pressure | 0 … 160 | bar | W ≥ 130, C ≥ 145 | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC AI 5.01 | Working pressure of the rudder actuator. Grows with rudder angle and ship speed. |
| `SG.OIL.TEMP` | Hydraulic oil temp | 10 … 90 | °C | W ≥ 60, C ≥ 70 | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC AI 5.02 | Hydraulic oil temperature in the steering gear tank. |
| `SG.OIL.LEVEL` | Hydraulic tank level | 0 … 100 | % | W ≤ 60, C ≤ 40 | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC AI 5.03 | Hydraulic tank level. SOLAS II-1/29 requires a low-level alarm to catch a leak before steering is lost. |
| `SG.PUMP1.RUN` | Pump 1 running | 0/1 |  |  | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC DI 5.01 | Steering pump 1 in service. |
| `SG.PUMP2.RUN` | Pump 2 running | 0/1 |  |  | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC DI 5.02 | Steering pump 2. Both pumps run together in restricted waters. |

## HVAC

Engine room ventilation and accommodation air conditioning.

| Tag | Point | Range | Unit | Alarm limits | Source | Address | Why it is monitored |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `HVAC.ER.TEMP` | Engine room air | 10 … 60 | °C | W ≥ 45, C ≥ 50 | NMEA 2000 | PGN 130312 source 3 | Engine room ambient. Hot air lowers engine output and cooks electronics; a fan failure shows here first. |
| `HVAC.ACC.TEMP` | Accommodation | 10 … 40 | °C | W ≥ 27, C ≥ 30 | NMEA 2000 | PGN 130312 source 2 | Accommodation air temperature. |
| `HVAC.OUT.TEMP` | Outside air | -20 … 45 | °C |  | NMEA 2000 | PGN 130312 source 1 | Outside air temperature at the ventilation intakes. |
| `HVAC.CHW.TEMP` | Chilled water supply | 0 … 20 | °C | W ≥ 11, C ≥ 14 | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC AI 6.01 | Chilled water leaving the A/C plant. Rises when a compressor trips. |

## Ballast System

Ballast tanks, pump and the list/trim they control.

| Tag | Point | Range | Unit | Alarm limits | Source | Address | Why it is monitored |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BW.FP.LEVEL` | Fore peak | 0 … 100 | % |  | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC AI 7.01 | Ballast tank level from the radar/pressure gauge. Used for stability and trim. |
| `BW.DB1P.LEVEL` | DB 1 port | 0 … 100 | % |  | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC AI 7.02 | Ballast tank level from the radar/pressure gauge. Used for stability and trim. |
| `BW.DB1S.LEVEL` | DB 1 stbd | 0 … 100 | % |  | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC AI 7.03 | Ballast tank level from the radar/pressure gauge. Used for stability and trim. |
| `BW.AP.LEVEL` | Aft peak | 0 … 100 | % |  | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC AI 7.04 | Ballast tank level from the radar/pressure gauge. Used for stability and trim. |
| `VSL.LIST` | List | -15 … 15 | ° | W \|x\| ≥ 5, C \|x\| ≥ 10 | Analog 4-20 mA | Inclinometer AI 7.10 (filtered) | Static list with the rolling filtered out, starboard positive. Unplanned list means water where it should not be. |
| `VSL.ROLL` | Roll angle | -30 … 30 | ° |  | Analog 4-20 mA | Inclinometer AI 7.10 | Instantaneous roll. Period and amplitude say a lot about sea state and stability. |
| `VSL.TRIM` | Trim | -3 … 3 | m |  | Calculated | aft draft - fore draft | Trim by the stern (positive). Wrong trim costs fuel. |
| `BW.PUMP.RUN` | Ballast pump running | 0/1 |  |  | Analog 4-20 mA | PLC DI 7.01 | Ballast pump in service. Normally stopped at sea. |
